mainTopic: Heating food on שבת with indirect heat: sun versus fire, the egg in hot cloths and sand, and the springs of טבריא
overview: This amud opens by finishing a proof: a ברייתא about rinsing salted fish shows that making food edible with even a little heat counts as cooking. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's argument about wrapping an egg in sun-heated cloths, which the רבנן forbid and רבי יוסי permits. רב נחמן explains that everyone permits using the sun directly and everyone forbids things heated by fire. The argument is only about things heated by the sun (תולדות החמה). Next the גמרא asks why רבי יוסי agrees to forbid burying an egg in sun-heated sand. רבה says it is a גזירה so people will not bury food in hot ashes, while רב יוסף says it is because the person moves earth, and the practical difference between them is loose earth. רב יוסף's reason is then challenged twice, from a hot roof and from the hot springs of טבריא, and both challenges are answered. The amud ends as רב חסדא begins a new statement that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from salted fish that light cooking counts as full cooking
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that rinsing very salty fish in hot water is enough to finish 'cooking' it. This proves that bringing food to an edible state counts as cooking, even if the heating is only light.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any salted food that was already put in hot water before שבת may be soaked in hot water on שבת. Anything that was not put in hot water before שבת may only be rinsed in hot water on שבת. The exception is old salted fish and Spanish colias fish, because rinsing them is already the completion of their 'work' (they become ready to eat). Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a proof it started on the previous amud. A ברייתא shows that even a quick rinse in hot water counts as cooking when that rinse makes the food ready to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous amud, the גמרא asked whether a slightly cooked egg counts as cooked. The ברייתא says that for certain fish, a simple rinse finishes their preparation, so the rinse itself is the forbidden act of cooking (בישול). The words 'שמע מינה' lock in the conclusion: making food edible with heat is cooking, even with very little heat.

keyTerms.meaning: soaking (leaving food sitting in the water)
rinsing (pouring water over quickly)
a type of small salted fish from Spain that is very soft
the completion of their 'work', meaning the act that finishes making them ready
'learn from it', a formula that confirms a proof

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think rinsing is always allowed. Rinsing is usually fine, but for these very soft fish the rinse itself finishes the cooking, so it is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule for the whole סוגיא: what counts as cooking is reaching edibility, not how long or how hard the food is heated.

phrases.english: Anything that came into hot water before Shabbat —
phrases.notes: Meaning it was already cooked before Shabbat.

phrases.english: one may soak it in hot water on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁלֹּא בָּא בְּחַמִּין מִלִּפְנֵי הַשַּׁבָּת —
phrases.english: and anything that did not come into hot water before Shabbat —
one may rinse it in hot water on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: Rinsing is allowed, but soaking is not.

phrases.english: except for old salted fish
and the colias fish of the Spaniards,
because rinsing them is itself the completion of their preparation.
Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof begun on the previous amud, about a slightly cooked egg.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that lightly cooking food to an edible state counts as the מלאכה of cooking.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about rinsing salted fish in hot water on שבת.

steps.title: Does the משנה allowing water in the sun follow only רבי יוסי?
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה says you may not wrap an egg in sun-heated cloths, but רבי יוסי allows it. Another משנה allows putting cold water in the sun to warm it. The גמרא asks whether that משנה follows only רבי יוסי and not the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה says: 'And one may not crack (cook) the egg by wrapping it in cloths.' Now, what about the משנה that teaches: one may put cooked food into a pit to protect it, good water into bad water to cool it, and cold water in the sun to warm it? Shall we say that this follows רבי יוסי and not the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of our משנה (wrapping the egg in hot cloths). It then asks whether another משנה, which lets you warm water in the sun, can only follow רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה the רבנן forbid heating an egg with sun-heated cloths, so they seem to forbid any use of the sun's heat. If so, the other משנה, which permits warming cold water in the sun, would fit only רבי יוסי. The גמרא prefers that a משנה fit everyone, so this question sets up רב נחמן's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: he cracks/cooks it, here meaning to make the egg cook through
cloths (here, cloths heated by the sun)
'and that which we learned', which introduces another משנה
'shall we say?', which proposes a possibly uncomfortable conclusion
in the sun

steps.confusionAlert: The first two cases (food in a pit, good water in bad water) are about protecting or cooling food. Only the third case, cold water in the sun, causes the problem here.

phrases.english: "And one may not crack it in cloths":
phrases.notes: Quote from our משנה. רבי יוסי permits this.

phrases.english: And that which we learned:
One may put a cooked dish into a pit
so that it will be preserved,
and good water into bad water
so that it will cool,
and cold water in the sun
so that it will warm up —

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא וְלָא רַבָּנַן?
phrases.english: shall we say it is Rabbi Yosei and not the Rabbis?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דִּתְנַן נוֹתְנִין תַּבְשִׁיל לְתוֹךְ הַבּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה (hot cloths) and opens a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the משנה permitting cold water in the sun follow only רבי יוסי, or can it fit the רבנן too?

steps.title: רב נחמן: the sun is permitted and fire-heated things are forbidden by all
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן lays out two zones that everyone agrees on: heating with the sun directly is permitted, and heating with something heated by fire is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: In the sun itself, everyone agrees it is permitted. With things heated by fire, everyone agrees it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן starts answering by marking out two cases with no argument. This prepares for his next line, which pins down where the real argument is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting water directly in the sun is not cooking at all, so even the רבנן allow it. This means the other משנה fits everyone. Heating with something that fire heated (תולדות האור) counts like fire itself, so everyone forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: everyone agrees (no one argues)
'offspring of fire': objects heated by fire
permitted
forbidden

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּחַמָּה — דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּשְׁרֵי.
phrases.english: In the sun — everyone agrees that it is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: בְּתוֹלְדוֹת הָאוּר — כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דַּאֲסִיר.
phrases.english: With derivatives of fire — everyone agrees that it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: בְּחַמָּה דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּשְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2: the sun itself is permitted even according to the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases: direct sun versus heated objects
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן forbid every kind of sun heating, so the other משנה must follow רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Direct sun is permitted by everyone, so the other משנה fits the רבנן too.

steps.title: The real argument is about things heated by the sun
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן and רבי יוסי argue only about objects heated by the sun, like the cloths. The רבנן make a גזירה because these look like fire-heated objects; רבי יוסי does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about things heated by the sun. One Sage holds we make a decree against sun-heated things because of fire-heated things, and the other Sage holds we do not make that decree.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן finishes his answer by naming the exact topic of the argument: things heated by the sun (תולדות החמה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sun-heated cloths look just like fire-heated cloths, and a person watching cannot tell the difference. So the רבנן forbid them as a protective decree (גזירה). רבי יוסי does not make this decree, so he allows the egg in sun-heated cloths.

keyTerms.meaning: 'offspring of the sun': objects heated by the sun
we make a rabbinic protective decree
because of (out of concern for)
'one master holds', used to present each side of an argument

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels. The sun itself is permitted by all. Fire-heated objects are forbidden by all. Sun-heated objects are argued about: the רבנן forbid them through a גזירה, and רבי יוסי permits them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This three-level framework is the basic rule for using indirect heat on שבת.

phrases.english: Where they argue is about derivatives of the sun:
One master holds that we decree
against derivatives of the sun because of derivatives of fire,
phrases.notes: This is the view of the רבנן.

phrases.english: and the other master holds that we do not decree.
phrases.notes: This is the view of רבי יוסי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב נחמן's answer by locating the dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the argument
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is limited to sun-heated objects, and it depends on whether we make a גזירה.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי יוסי also permit burying an egg in hot sand?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids burying an egg in sun-heated sand, and no one argues. The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי does not disagree here too, since sand heated by the sun is also a sun-heated object.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one may not bury it in sand.' Let רבי יוסי argue about this too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and challenges it. Based on רב נחמן, רבי יוסי should permit hot sand as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sun-heated sand is a תולדת החמה, just like the cloths. Since רבי יוסי does not decree against sun-heated things, his silence here is puzzling. Why would he agree to forbid this?

keyTerms.meaning: he buries/insulates it (to cook it in the heat)
sand
'let him argue', used to ask why someone does not disagree

phrases.english: "And one may not bury it in sand":
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה, about sand heated by the sun.

phrases.english: Let Rabbi Yosei argue about this too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב נחמן's framework to challenge the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that רבי יוסי agrees to forbid burying an egg in sun-heated sand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sand heated by the sun is a תולדת החמה, and רבי יוסי permits those, so he should permit this too.

steps.title: רבה: a decree so people won't bury food in hot ashes
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that sand is different. Burying food in hot sand looks just like burying it in hot ashes (רמץ), which is real fire-heat. So even רבי יוסי forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It is a decree, in case he comes to bury it in hot ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a first answer. Sand has a special decree of its own that even רבי יוסי accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hot ashes come from fire, so burying food in them is forbidden by everyone. The act of burying in sand and in ashes looks identical, so allowing sand could lead people to use ashes. This concern is stronger than the cloth case, which is why רבי יוסי agrees here.

keyTerms.meaning: a decree in case (out of fear that) a person will do something
hot ashes still holding heat from fire

phrases.english: Rabbah said:
It is a decree, lest he bury it in hot ashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר: גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא יַטְמִין בְּרֶמֶץ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sand is just another sun-heated object that רבי יוסי should permit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sand is forbidden because it could lead to burying food in hot ashes.

steps.title: רב יוסף: burying moves dirt out of its place
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a different reason that has nothing to do with heat. Burying the egg pushes earth aside, which is like digging, and that is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Because he moves earth from its place.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a second, different answer to the same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב יוסף, the problem is not cooking at all. Pressing the egg into the ground displaces earth, which looks like digging a hole. So רבי יוסי can agree to forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: moves, displaces
earth, dirt

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Because he moves earth from its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמֵּזִיז עָפָר מִמְּקוֹמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to the challenge in step 5, in place of רבה's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate prohibition (moving earth), not about heating
steps.terutzMaskana: The sand case is forbidden because of displacing earth, so it has nothing to do with the cloth argument.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between רבה and רב יוסף?
steps.stepSummary: Since both forbid burying the egg in sand, the גמרא asks what practical case they would disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next step by asking for a case where the two reasons would give different rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the normal case both reasons lead to the same result: forbidden. The גמרא wants a case where only one of the reasons applies.

keyTerms.meaning: 'what is between them?', asking for the practical difference between two opinions

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers in steps 6 and 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where רבה and רב יוסף would rule differently.

steps.title: The difference is loose earth
steps.stepSummary: With loose, crumbly earth (עפר תיחוח), nothing is really dug up, so רב יוסף would permit it. רבה would still forbid it because of the hot-ash concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: loose earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions split in the case of loose earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pushing an egg into loose earth does not count as moving earth, so רב יוסף's reason does not apply and it would be permitted. רבה's concern about hot ashes still applies, so he forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'there is between them', which introduces the practical difference
loose, soft earth that does not need digging

steps.whatToRemember: Even רבי יוסי forbids burying an egg in sun-heated sand. רבה says the reason is concern about hot ashes, so even loose earth is forbidden. רב יוסף says the reason is moving earth, so loose earth is permitted.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: loose earth.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Loose earth: רב יוסף permits it (no earth is moved), and רבה forbids it (the hot-ash decree still applies).

steps.title: A hot rooftop seems to challenge רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows rolling an egg on a sun-heated roof but forbids it on boiling lime. That fits רבה, but why doesn't רב יוסף forbid the roof too, since moving earth could happen there?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says you may roll an egg on a hot roof, but not on boiling lime. This makes sense for the one who said the reason is a גזירה, a protective rule against hiding food in hot ashes, since a roof looks nothing like ashes. But for the one who said the reason is moving earth, shouldn't he forbid the roof too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא and uses it to challenge רב יוסף's reason, which is moving earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A roof is nothing like hot ashes, so רבה has no reason to forbid it. But a roof can have some earth on it, so רב יוסף should seemingly forbid rolling an egg there. The ברייתא allows it with no conditions, which looks like a problem for רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (usually from a ברייתא or משנה)
Roll an egg on something hot to lightly roast it
A roof made very hot by the sun
Hot lime. Its heat is treated as fire-heat (תולדות האור), not sun-heat, which is why the egg may not be rolled on it
'Granted for this view… but for that view' — the standard pattern for attacking only one side

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: מְגַלְגְּלִין בֵּיצָה עַל גַּבֵּי גַּג רוֹתֵחַ,
phrases.english: One may roll an egg on top of a sun-heated roof,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְגַלְגְּלִין בֵּיצָה עַל גַּבֵּי סִיד רוֹתֵחַ.
phrases.english: but one may not roll an egg on top of boiling lime.
Granted, according to the one who said
it is a decree lest he bury it in hot ashes —
there is no reason to make a decree here.
phrases.notes: A roof does not look like ashes.

phrases.english: But according to the one who said
it is because he moves earth from its place, let him decree here too?
phrases.notes: Sometimes a roof has earth on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the disagreement defined in step 9 against an outside ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A roof can have earth on it, so rolling an egg there could involve moving earth. Yet רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits it without any condition.

steps.title: An ordinary roof has no earth
steps.stepSummary: Roofs normally have no earth on them, so there is no reason to forbid the roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: A regular roof has no earth on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יוסף by explaining that a normal roof has no earth to move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's concern only applies where there is earth. The ברייתא is describing the usual roof, which is bare. חז"ל do not make rules for unusual cases.

keyTerms.meaning: The ordinary, usual case
It has no earth on it

phrases.english: — An ordinary roof has no earth on it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the typical case so the concern does not apply
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A roof might have earth on it, so rolling an egg there should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: A normal roof has no earth, so רב יוסף agrees it is allowed.

steps.title: The pipe of טבריא seems to challenge רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: The people of טבריא ran a cold-water pipe through hot spring water and were forbidden to use it. That looks like הטמנה, but no earth was moved, so how does רב יוסף explain it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the people of טבריא brought a pipe of cold water through a channel of hot water, and so on. This makes sense for the one who says the reason is a גזירה against hiding food in ashes, because this looks like הטמנה. But for the one who says the reason is moving earth, what can he say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to רב יוסף, from the story of טבריא that comes right after the egg case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the story sits right next to the sand case, it seems to explain it. The pipe surrounded by hot water looks like burying food, so it fits רבה. But no earth is moved there, so רב יוסף's reason cannot explain why it was forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear — introduces a source used as a proof or a challenge
A pipe
A channel of hot spring water
Burying or wrapping food to keep it hot or to heat it

phrases.english: Come and hear:
An incident that the people of Tiberias did,
and they brought a pipe of cold water
into a channel of hot water, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on to say the חכמים forbade them.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who said
it is a decree lest he bury it in hot ashes —
that is why it was forbidden: it resembles burying.
But according to the one who said
it is because he moves earth from its place —
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָשׂוּ אַנְשֵׁי טְבֶרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רב יוסף after the first one was answered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The story comes right after the sand case and seems to share its reason. Yet it involves no earth at all, so only רבה's 'looks like הטמנה' reason can explain it.

steps.title: The טבריא story belongs to the earlier dispute
steps.stepSummary: The story of טבריא is not about the sand case at the end of the משנה. It belongs to the earlier part, where the חכמים and רבי יוסי argue about wrapping an egg in cloths.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think the story of טבריא refers to the last part of the משנה? It refers to the first part: 'One may not wrap the egg in cloths, and רבי יוסי permits it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the challenge rests on a wrong assumption about which part of the משנה the story belongs to. It then sets up how the story fits into the earlier dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the story is not about the sand case, it cannot tell us the reason for the sand rule. That means it is no challenge to רב יוסף. Instead, it is attached to the argument about sun-heated cloths.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think…? — introduces a rejection of the questioner's assumption
The last clause of a משנה
The first clause of a משנה
Wrap the egg in sun-heated cloths so it cooks

steps.confusionAlert: Beginners often assume a story printed right after a rule must explain that exact rule. Here the גמרא says it actually goes back to the earlier clause of the משנה.

phrases.english: Do you think
that the Tiberias incident refers to the last clause?
It refers to the first clause:
'One may not wrap it in cloths,'
'and Rabbi Yosei permits it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ מַעֲשֶׂה טְבֶרְיָא אַסֵּיפָא קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by moving the story to a different clause of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-placing the source within the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The טבריא story explains the sand rule, so it must reflect רבה's reasoning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The story belongs to the dispute about cloths and says nothing about why burying in sand is forbidden.

steps.title: The חכמים use טבריא to challenge רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים tell רבי יוסי that the springs of טבריא are heated by the sun, and yet the water was forbidden. So sun-heated cloths should be forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the חכמים said to רבי יוסי: the incident of the people of טבריא involved something heated by the sun, and the חכמים still forbade it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the story fits into the earlier dispute. The חכמים use it to argue against רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי permits sun-heated cloths because the heat does not come from fire. The חכמים answer that the hot springs also seem to be heated without fire, yet the water was forbidden. So sun-heated things should be forbidden as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Things heated by the sun, not by fire
And this is what they were saying — explains the meaning of a quoted exchange

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכִי קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: And this is what the Rabbis said to Rabbi Yosei:
Wasn't the incident of the people of Tiberias
a case of something heated by the sun,
and yet the Sages forbade it to them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכִי קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer of step 13 by spelling out the exchange inside the earlier dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's ruling that sun-heated cloths are allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The springs of טבריא are heated by the sun, and the water was still forbidden. So things heated by the sun should not be allowed.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the springs of טבריא are heated by fire
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers that the springs of טבריא are heated by fire, because they pass over the entrance to גיהנם. So the story says nothing about sun-heated things.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: that water is heated by fire, because it passes over the entrance to גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי rejects the חכמים' comparison by saying the springs are actually heated by fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the springs are heated by fire, forbidding them fits רבי יוסי's view that only fire-heat is a problem. So the story does not disprove his ruling about sun-heated cloths. It also stays unconnected to the sand case, which ends the challenge to רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: Things heated by fire
The entrance to גיהנם, a real underground fire
They pass over

steps.whatToRemember: Both challenges to רב יוסף fail. The roof normally has no earth, and the טבריא story belongs to the dispute about cloths, where רבי יוסי explains the springs are heated by fire. So the disagreement between רבה and רב יוסף remains in place.

phrases.english: He said to them:
That is a case of something heated by fire,
for they pass over the entrance to Gehenna.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הַהוּא תּוֹלְדוֹת אוּר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוסי answers the חכמים' challenge from step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the heat comes from fire, not from the sun
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The springs of טבריא are heated by the sun, so their prohibition should cover all sun-heated things.
steps.terutzMaskana: The springs are heated by the fires of גיהנם, so the prohibition fits רבי יוסי's view.

steps.title: רב חסדא begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a statement of רב חסדא on the same topic. The statement itself continues on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line: the גמרא is introducing a statement of רב חסדא. The statement itself appears on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the attribution appears here. The actual teaching of רב חסדא belongs to the next passage and should be read together with this line.
